title: Wrap TrackLearningOrderDao.upsertOrder's per-row insert loop and its repository call sites in one transaction/batch

why: upsertOrder writes N rows via an awaited for-loop with no db.transaction()/db.batch() wrapper, and its only callers (saveSedarimOrder/saveMasechtosOrder/resetToDefault) then make a second, entirely separate write (stampReorderAt) with no shared transaction either. A user reordering a full masechta/seder (which can be dozens to hundreds of refs) who has the app killed mid-reorder (OS memory pressure, backgrounding kill — routine on mobile) is left with a partially-old/partially-new sortOrder sequence and no error anywhere. getByTrack() then feeds that corrupted order straight into the daily learning projection, producing skipped or repeated study segments with zero user-visible signal that anything went wrong. Even when upsertOrder itself completes, dying before the separate stampReorderAt call leaves a stale lastReorderAt, breaking the reorder-amnesty logic documented at architecture §10.1. This is discovered via track_learning_order_dao_test.dart (in this batch), which covers the happy path only and has no test for interrupted/partial writes.
recommendation: Replace the for-loop in upsertOrder with a single db.batch((b) { for (...) b.insert(trackLearningOrder, ..., onConflict: ...); }) — Drift batches are atomic, satisfying DB-2 and DB-3 in one change. In the repository, wrap the order-write + stampReorderAt call of saveSedarimOrder/saveMasechtosOrder/resetToDefault in one _database.transaction(...) so the pair commits or rolls back together.
acceptance_criteria: TrackLearningOrderDao.upsertOrder issues one db.batch() instead of an awaited per-row loop.
saveSedarimOrder, saveMasechtosOrder, and resetToDefault each wrap their order-write + stampReorderAt call in a single db.transaction().
New regression test asserts the reorder write is all-or-nothing (e.g. inject a failure partway through a multi-ref batch and assert zero rows changed / the pre-reorder order is intact).

No Rule-0 checker exists yet for this class of bug (DB-2/DB-3 are [P]ending) — note the gap; a grep for `for (` followed within a few lines by `await into(` or `await (db.update`/`await (db.delete` inside lib/core/database/daos/**/*.dart would catch this pattern cheaply.

corrections: Note for orchestrator (not a reason to kill): a closely related/possibly overlapping finding exists elsewhere in the audit (grp-117 'Wrap saveOrder/resetToDefault's reorder-amnesty stamp in the same transaction as the order write', and grp-115) covering the same stampReorderAt-not-in-transaction defect from a different chunk -- worth deduping against high-007's DB-2 portion during merge, though high-007 additionally and correctly captures the distinct DB-3 per-row-loop defect in upsertOrder that those do not.
